questions.stem:
The GST Council has been in the news over proposed reforms to registration and dispute resolution. Consider the following statements about the GST Council:
1. It is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Constitution.
2. It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes the Finance Ministers of all States as members.
3. The recommendations of the GST Council are legally binding on both the Union and State Governments.
4. The Council is serviced administratively by the GST Council Secretariat.
How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: It is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Constitution.
It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes the Finance Ministers of all States as members.
The recommendations of the GST Council are legally binding on both the Union and State Governments.
The Council is serviced administratively by the GST Council Secretariat.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are factually correct. Statement 3 is wrong: in Mohit Minerals v. Union of India (2022), the Supreme Court held that GST Council recommendations are only recommendatory and persuasive, not binding, since both Parliament and State legislatures retain simultaneous power to legislate on GST under Article 246A.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: GST Council meeting postponed for second time, rescheduled to October 8
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 279A and cooperative federalism, similar to UPSC 2023 question on GST Council powers and the binding nature of its recommendations.

questions.stem:
With reference to the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026, awarded for discoveries in optogenetics, consider the following statements:
1. It is awarded by the Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute.
2. Optogenetics uses light-gated ion channels to selectively control the activity of specific neurons.
3. The 2026 Prize in Physiology or Medicine was shared among three laureates.
4. All Nobel Prizes, including the one in Economic Sciences, are funded from Alfred Nobel's original 1895 bequest.
How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: It is awarded by the Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute.
Optogenetics uses light-gated ion channels to selectively control the activity of specific neurons.
The 2026 Prize in Physiology or Medicine was shared among three laureates.
All Nobel Prizes, including the one in Economic Sciences, are funded from Alfred Nobel's original 1895 bequest.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — the 2026 Medicine Prize went jointly to Deisseroth, Hegeman and Nagel for light-gated ion channels and optogenetics, and the Medicine Prize is indeed awarded via the Karolinska Institute. Statement 4 is wrong: the Prize in Economic Sciences is the Sveriges Riksbank Prize, instituted in 1968 by Sweden's central bank and funded separately from Nobel's original bequest.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: The Nobel-winning science of optogenetics: Explained
questions.pyqLink: Static concept: mechanism of optogenetics and the institutional structure of the Nobel Prizes, an area UPSC has tested via science-award current affairs trigger questions.

questions.stem:
With reference to the Great Indian Bustard, recently in the news after a captive-bred release in Rajasthan, consider the following statements:
1. It is classified as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List and is listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
2. It is primarily a species of dense forest habitats and depends on tall tree canopies for nesting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: It is classified as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List and is listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
It is primarily a species of dense forest habitats and depends on tall tree canopies for nesting.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct; the bustard's critically low population and legal protection are well established. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Great Indian Bustard is a grassland and arid-scrubland species that nests on open ground, which is precisely why it is vulnerable to collision with overhead power lines strung across its open habitat.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Two captive-bred Great Indian Bustards released into wild in Rajasthan under conservation efforts
questions.pyqLink: Tests grassland-ecosystem habitat requirements and conservation status, similar to UPSC's recurring species-habitat questions (e.g., 2020 Great Indian Bustard question).

questions.stem:
The Union Cabinet is set to consider a proposal to create an Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) as a Special Purpose Vehicle. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. The ITLA is proposed to be set up as a non-profit special purpose vehicle under the Companies Act, 2013.
2. It will function under the administrative control of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, since that ministry proposed it.
3. A company registered under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 is prohibited from distributing dividends to its members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The ITLA is proposed to be set up as a non-profit special purpose vehicle under the Companies Act, 2013.
It will function under the administrative control of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, since that ministry proposed it.
A company registered under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 is prohibited from distributing dividends to its members.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct, as the ITLA is to be set up as a non-profit SPV under the Companies Act, 2013. Statement 3 is correct as a general static fact about Section 8 companies. Statement 2 is incorrect: despite being proposed by the Commerce Ministry, the body is to function under the administrative control of the Cabinet Secretariat, not the Commerce Ministry.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Union Cabinet to take up ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund, centralised infra authority
questions.pyqLink: Tests distinction between statutory, constitutional and company-law (Section 8 SPV) bodies — a recurring UPSC institutional-classification theme.

questions.stem:
Consider the following pairs of locations/sites mentioned in recent news and the State in which each is situated:

Site : State
1. Desert National Park : Rajasthan
2. Great Nicobar Island : Andaman and Nicobar Islands
3. Malarikkal (pink water lily habitat) : Tamil Nadu
4. Sam and Ramdevra (Great Indian Bustard breeding centres) : Rajasthan

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Sam and Ramdevra (Great Indian Bustard breeding centres)
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correctly matched — Desert National Park and the GIB breeding centres of Sam and Ramdevra are in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, and Great Nicobar Island is part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Union Territory. Pair 3 is incorrect: Malarikkal, known for its pink water lily blooms, is located in Kottayam district, Kerala, not Tamil Nadu.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Two captive-bred Great Indian Bustards released into wild in Rajasthan under conservation efforts
questions.pyqLink: Tests location-based mapping of protected areas and Union Territories, a recurring UPSC 'places in news' pattern.

questions.stem: The upcoming GST Council meeting is expected to discuss streamlining the input tax credit disbursement mechanism. With reference to the Goods and Services Tax regime, which one of the following best describes 'Input Tax Credit'?
options: It is a cess levied on luxury and sin goods to compensate States for GST revenue loss.
It is the credit a registered taxpayer can claim for tax already paid on inputs, which is set off against the tax liability on output supply to avoid cascading of taxes.
It is the turnover threshold below which small businesses are exempted from mandatory GST registration.
It is the refund of customs duty paid on inputs used in the manufacture of exported goods.
questions.explanation: Input Tax Credit (ITC) is the core mechanism by which GST avoids a cascading 'tax on tax' effect, letting a taxable person reduce the tax paid on purchases from the tax payable on sales. Option (a) describes the GST Compensation Cess, (c) describes the registration threshold limit, and (d) describes duty drawback under customs law — all are distinct, near-miss concepts under indirect taxation.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: GST Council meeting rescheduled for Thursday, says official order
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static GST mechanism, similar in style to UPSC 2019's 'Merchant Discount Rate' best-describes question.

questions.stem:
In the context of the Supreme Court's observations while refusing to stay proceedings on the Great Nicobar project, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Supreme Court observed that preservation of the culture of indigenous tribal communities is a fundamental right protected under the Constitution.
Statement-II: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognises the individual and community forest rights of forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
statements: The Supreme Court observed that preservation of the culture of indigenous tribal communities is a fundamental right protected under the Constitution.
The Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognises the individual and community forest rights of forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are independently factually correct. However, Statement-II does not explain Statement-I: the Court's observation on cultural preservation flows from fundamental rights jurisprudence under Articles 21 and 29, not from the statutory scheme of the Forest Rights Act, which is a separate legislative recognition of forest-dweller rights.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Supreme Court refuses to stay proceedings against Nicobar project
questions.pyqLink: Tests the distinction between constitutional fundamental rights and statutory protections for tribal communities, a theme UPSC has tested since the 2022-style Statement-I/II introduction.

questions.stem: With reference to the preparation and revision of electoral rolls in India, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: The electoral rolls used in India are prepared and revised, including through a Special Intensive Revision, under powers traceable to Article 324 of the Constitution read with the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

Statement-II: Article 324 vests in the Election Commission of India the superintendence, direction and control of elections, a mandate that extends to the preparation of electoral rolls in the absence of a specific parliamentary law occupying the field.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Article 324 gives ECI the general power of superintendence, direction and control of elections, which courts have held covers electoral roll matters not specifically covered by the Representation of the People Act, 1950; the SIR exercise and the opposition's objections to it (seen in the ECI march) rest on this constitutional-cum-statutory basis. Statement-II correctly states the source of that power, making it the explanation for Statement-I.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: CEC row LIVE updates: INDIA bloc MPs march to ECI in Delhi, demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 324 and ECI's constitutional mandate; similar to UPSC's recurring Statement-I/II questions on constitutional bodies since 2022.

questions.stem: With reference to agencies investigating economic offences in India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Enforcement Directorate investigates offences under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, which deals with proceeds of crime.
The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption is a Central Government agency responsible for investigating corruption cases involving Central Government employees.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the ED's mandate under the PMLA, 2002 covers tracing and attaching proceeds of crime, as seen in its sand-mining case referral. Statement 2 is incorrect: the DVAC is a State-level anti-corruption agency (here, Tamil Nadu's), not a Central Government body; the Central equivalent for central employees is the CBI's Anti-Corruption Branch, working with the CVC.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: DVAC launches probe into the alleged sand mining scam during the DMK government
questions.pyqLink: Tests statutory vs jurisdictional distinction between Central (ED/CBI) and State (DVAC/ACB) anti-corruption bodies, a recurring institutional-detail theme in UPSC Economy/Polity sets.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the regulation of water pollution from industrial effluents in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 provides the statutory basis for the constitution of State Pollution Control Boards.
An industrial unit is permitted to discharge untreated effluents into a water body provided the volume discharged is below a prescribed threshold.
The Central Pollution Control Board functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
Under the 'Polluter Pays' principle recognised by Indian courts, an industry causing water pollution is liable to bear the cost of remedying the damage caused.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct: the Water Act, 1974 creates State Boards, the CPCB works under MoEFCC, and the Polluter Pays principle was affirmed in cases like Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum. Statement 2 is false — no industry may discharge effluents, treated or not, without the prior 'consent to discharge' of the State Pollution Control Board, regardless of volume, which is exactly the violation alleged in the Guruganga stream pollution.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: 'Save Guruganga' campaign reaches Bidar
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Water Act 1974 framework and Polluter Pays principle, static concepts regularly triggered by river/stream pollution news items.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: It mandates that a Data Fiduciary intimate the Data Protection Board of India and the affected individuals in the event of a personal data breach.
It applies only to processing of digital personal data within the territory of India and not to such processing outside India.
It establishes the Data Protection Board of India with powers to impose financial penalties for non-compliance.
'Significant Data Fiduciaries' under the Act are exempted from the requirement of appointing a Data Protection Officer.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — breach intimation to the Board and affected Data Principals, and the Board's penalty powers, are both provided in the Act. Statement 2 is wrong: the Act has extraterritorial reach, applying also to processing outside India if connected with offering goods or services to Data Principals in India (relevant to how global AI agents from firms like Anthropic or OpenAI handling Indian users' data would be covered). Statement 4 is wrong: Significant Data Fiduciaries are specifically required, not exempted, to appoint a Data Protection Officer.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Anthropic tells Australia it's open to laws requiring reporting of AI agent hacks
questions.pyqLink: Tests DPDP Act 2023 provisions on breach notification, extraterritorial scope and Significant Data Fiduciary obligations, triggered by global debate on AI-agent data breaches.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of monuments and the dynasty under which they were built:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The first three pairs are correctly matched: the Thousand Pillar Temple (whose Dwarapala sculptures are now under ASI restoration) and the Ramappa Temple were both built in the Kakatiya period, the Hoysaleswara Temple under the Hoysalas, and the Brihadisvara Temple under the Cholas. The fourth pair is wrong — the Ramappa Temple at Palampet, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was built under the Kakatiya dynasty (under general Recharla Rudra), not the Chalukyas.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: ASI undertakes Dwarapala restoration at Thousand Pillar Temple in Telangana’s Hanumakonda
questions.pyqLink: Tests dynasty-monument association for Deccan temple architecture, a frequent pairs-matched theme since the Ramappa Temple's 2021 UNESCO inscription.

questions.stem: Andhra Pradesh's Annamayya district recorded a sharp monsoon rainfall deficit this season, which officials attributed partly to El Nino conditions. With reference to El Nino, which one of the following best describes the phenomenon?
options: A periodic warming of sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean that weakens trade winds and is generally associated with below-normal monsoon rainfall over India

A periodic cooling of sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean that strengthens trade winds and is generally associated with above-normal monsoon rainfall over India
A difference in sea-surface temperature between the western and eastern Indian Ocean that independently influences the strength of the Indian monsoon
A periodic reversal of surface atmospheric pressure between the eastern Pacific and the Indo-Australian region, unconnected with any change in sea-surface temperature
questions.explanation: El Nino is the warm phase of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation, marked by anomalous warming of the central-eastern equatorial Pacific and weakened trade winds, and is statistically linked to deficient Indian monsoon rainfall — consistent with Annamayya's 51% deficit. Option b describes La Nina (the opposite, wetter phase); option c describes the Indian Ocean Dipole, a separate Indian Ocean phenomenon; option d wrongly strips the Southern Oscillation of its sea-surface-temperature linkage.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Overnight rain brings relief to Annamayya, but the district’s monsoon deficit stands at 51%
questions.pyqLink: Tests El Nino/La Nina/IOD distinction, a recurring Geography concept triggered by monsoon-deficit news.

questions.stem: With reference to India's maritime capability and strategic outreach in the Indian Ocean, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: 'Security and Growth for All in the Region' (SAGAR) is India's vision for maritime cooperation and security in the Indian Ocean Region.
Fleet Support Ships enhance a navy's operational reach by replenishing fuel and stores to warships at sea, reducing the need for them to return to port.
India is a member of the Indian Ocean Rim Association, a regional grouping promoting economic and security cooperation among Indian Ocean littoral states.
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. SAGAR, articulated in 2015, remains India's guiding doctrine for the Indian Ocean Region; Fleet Support Ships such as the newly launched INS Surya perform exactly the at-sea replenishment role described, extending naval endurance for both combat and diplomatic/HADR missions; and India has been a founding member of IORA since 1997.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Rajnath Singh launches Navy's first indigenous fleet support ship 'Surya' at Visakhapatnam
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's Indian Ocean strategic initiatives (SAGAR, IORA) and naval logistics capability, concepts regularly anchored to naval commissioning news.

questions.stem: A Chhattisgarh Gram Sabha in Sukma district recently cited the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) to pass a resolution denying burial land to tribal Christians. With reference to the Fifth Schedule and PESA, consider the following statements: 1. PESA, 1996 extends the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution to Scheduled Areas with certain exceptions and modifications. 2. The Fifth Schedule to the Constitution applies automatically to all Scheduled Tribe-dominated areas in the north-eastern States. 3. The powers given to the Gram Sabha under PESA to safeguard community customs and traditions cannot be used to override Fundamental Rights such as freedom of religion guaranteed under Article 25. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: PESA, 1996 extends the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution to Scheduled Areas with certain exceptions and modifications.
The Fifth Schedule to the Constitution applies automatically to all Scheduled Tribe-dominated areas in the north-eastern States.
The powers given to the Gram Sabha under PESA to safeguard community customs and traditions cannot be used to override Fundamental Rights such as freedom of religion guaranteed under Article 25.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — PESA extends Part IX panchayat provisions to Fifth Schedule Areas with modifications. Statement 2 is wrong — Scheduled Tribe areas in the north-east (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram) are governed by the Sixth Schedule under Article 244(2), not the Fifth Schedule, which applies to states like Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Jharkhand. Statement 3 is correct — a Gram Sabha's customary powers under Section 4(d) of PESA are subordinate legislation and cannot override Part III Fundamental Rights such as Article 25, which is the core constitutional issue in the Sukma burial-land dispute.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: 'No land for burial': Chhattisgarh village resolution raises concerns for Christians
questions.pyqLink: Tests Fifth vs Sixth Schedule distinction and PESA's Gram Sabha powers; similar to UPSC 2015/2018 questions on Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act and Fifth Schedule areas

questions.stem: The Chief Justice of India recently observed that the Supreme Court had not approved any modification to Form 6, after the Election Commission added a new column to it ahead of a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. With reference to this, consider the following statements: 1. Form 6, prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, is the form used by a citizen to apply for inclusion of their name in the electoral roll of a constituency. 2. The Election Commission's power to conduct a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls flows directly from Article 324 of the Constitution and requires no backing from the Representation of the People Act, 1950. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Form 6, prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, is the form used by a citizen to apply for inclusion of their name in the electoral roll of a constituency.

The Election Commission's power to conduct a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls flows directly from Article 324 of the Constitution and requires no backing from the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — Form 6 under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 is the statutory form for inclusion of a new or shifted elector's name. Statement 2 is incorrect — revision of electoral rolls, including a Special/Intensive Revision, is carried out under Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950; Article 324 gives the EC general superintendence but is not a substitute for this statutory basis, which is precisely why courts scrutinise changes like the Form 6 modification.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Rahul Gandhi says abuse of position by CEC Gyanesh Kumar proven, BJP calls remarks ‘full of lies’
questions.pyqLink: Tests statutory basis of electoral roll revision (RP Act 1950) vs Article 324 superintendence powers of the Election Commission

questions.stem: Odisha's rising paddy procurement, driven by MSP hikes, has left the state with surplus rice stocks awaiting storage. With reference to India's foodgrain procurement and management system, consider the following statements: 1. The Minimum Support Price (MSP) for paddy is recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) and announced by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs. 2. The Food Corporation of India procures rice both directly and through the custom milling route, under which paddy procured by state agencies is milled into rice and delivered to the FCI. 3. Buffer stock norms for foodgrains are fixed by the Reserve Bank of India to control food inflation. 4. Under the Decentralized Procurement Scheme, state governments can themselves procure, store and distribute foodgrains for the Public Distribution System with central assistance. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The Minimum Support Price (MSP) for paddy is recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) and announced by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
The Food Corporation of India procures rice both directly and through the custom milling route, under which paddy procured by state agencies is milled into rice and delivered to the FCI.
Buffer stock norms for foodgrains are fixed by the Reserve Bank of India to control food inflation.
Under the Decentralized Procurement Scheme, state governments can themselves procure, store and distribute foodgrains for the Public Distribution System with central assistance.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct and describe how MSP is set, how custom milling converts procured paddy into rice for the FCI (as in Odisha's case), and how the Decentralized Procurement Scheme lets states manage their own procurement. Statement 3 is incorrect — buffer stock and strategic reserve norms are fixed by the Department of Food and Public Distribution (Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution), not the RBI, which has no role in physical foodgrain stock management.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Odisha to create additional storage for rice to accommodate paddy glut
questions.pyqLink: Tests MSP mechanism, FCI procurement routes and buffer stock norms, a recurring UPSC theme on food management since 2020

questions.stem: India and Switzerland have agreed to deepen cooperation in the nuclear energy sector. With reference to India's nuclear power programme, consider the following statements: 1. Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs), used in the first stage of India's nuclear power programme, run on enriched uranium imported entirely from foreign suppliers. 2. In the second and third stages of India's nuclear power programme, fast breeder reactors and thorium-based reactors are envisaged, given India's large thorium reserves. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs), used in the first stage of India's nuclear power programme, run on enriched uranium imported entirely from foreign suppliers.
In the second and third stages of India's nuclear power programme, fast breeder reactors and thorium-based reactors are envisaged, given India's large thorium reserves.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct — Homi Bhabha's three-stage nuclear power programme moves from PHWRs to fast breeder reactors using plutonium, and finally to thorium-based reactors, since India holds one of the world's largest thorium reserves. Statement 1 is incorrect — PHWRs use natural (unenriched) uranium as fuel, much of it sourced domestically, which is precisely why India's first stage was designed around its limited uranium but abundant thorium resources.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: India, Switzerland to strengthen ties in defence, nuclear energy sectors
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's three-stage nuclear power programme and reactor fuel types, a recurring static topic linked to nuclear energy cooperation news

questions.stem: A plaque was unveiled in Mumbai in memory of Ramnath Goenka, founder of The Indian Express. With reference to newspapers associated with India's freedom struggle and press history, consider the following pairs: Newspaper : Associated Personality 1. Indian Express : Ramnath Goenka 2. Kesari : Bal Gangadhar Tilak 3. Young India : Lala Lajpat Rai 4. Harijan : Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — Ramnath Goenka founded The Indian Express in 1932, and Tilak founded the Marathi weekly Kesari in 1881. Pair 3 is wrong — Young India was edited by Mahatma Gandhi, not Lala Lajpat Rai, who is associated with papers like Bande Mataram and The People. Pair 4 is wrong — Harijan was also founded and edited by Mahatma Gandhi; Ambedkar's journals were Mooknayak and Bahishkrit Bharat.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Plaque in tribute to Indian Express group founder Ramnath Goenka unveiled at Nariman Point in Mumbai
questions.pyqLink: Tests newspapers and journals associated with freedom-struggle leaders, a recurring UPSC pairs-matching theme on nationalist press

questions.stem: Odisha has recorded a massive paddy harvest in recent years, forcing the state to expand rice storage capacity. With reference to paddy cultivation along India's eastern coast, which one of the following best describes why states like Odisha, West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh are among the country's largest rice producers?
options: These states lie in the rain-shadow region of the Western Ghats, which assures them steady rainfall ideal for a water-intensive kharif crop like paddy.
These states receive the bulk of their rainfall from winter western disturbances, which coincides with the paddy transplantation season.
Rice cultivation in these states depends primarily on groundwater extraction through tube wells, as in the Indo-Gangetic plains of Punjab and Haryana.
The fertile alluvial soil of river deltas such as the Mahanadi, combined with heavy south-west monsoon rainfall and an extensive canal-irrigation network, supports paddy as the dominant kharif crop.
questions.explanation: Option 4 is correct — the Mahanadi, Godavari and Krishna-Godavari deltas have fertile alluvial soil, assured high rainfall from the south-west monsoon, and canal networks (e.g., Hirakud) that together make paddy the dominant kharif crop of the eastern coastal states. Option 1 is wrong because these states lie on the windward, not rain-shadow, side of peninsular India; option 2 wrongly links paddy transplantation (a monsoon-season, June-September activity) to winter western disturbances; option 3 wrongly attributes a canal-and-delta-irrigated region's farming to Punjab-style groundwater-based cultivation.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Odisha to create additional storage for rice to accommodate paddy glut
questions.pyqLink: Tests agro-climatic basis of rice cultivation and deltaic agriculture on India's eastern coast, a recurring UPSC geography-of-agriculture theme

articles.title: Single-window GST registration for multistate businesses set for pilot this week
articles.summary: In a significant move, the central government is set to implement a consolidated goods and services tax registration system for businesses operating across multiple states.
